title: Noradrenergic Signalling
mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
rationale: Retain historical noradrenaline-related capacity decisions; review separates precursor/PLP supply from actual norepinephrine synthesis/release. Exact receptor/state and dietary exposure claims deferred.

data.title: Noradrenergic Signalling
data.mission: Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged.
data.summary: Noradrenaline, also called norepinephrine, helps set arousal, vigilance and executive control so attention can stay engaged. Neurons make it from dopamine, then shape the signal through release, receptors, reuptake and breakdown. This coordination lets alertness follow cognitive demand. Iron, vitamin B6, copper and vitamin C take part in that chemistry.
data.dose_sensitivity: Pattern-based; adequate protein plus cofactor sufficiency
data.scientific_findings_intro: Structural and biochemical evidence establishes copper and ascorbate participation in the defining dopamine-to-noradrenaline conversion. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) Animal pharmacology and neuronal recordings separately support receptor-dependent prefrontal regulation and firing-pattern responses to attended cues. [[16]](#pm-ref-16) [[18]](#pm-ref-18) These findings support distinct synthesis and signalling processes; they do not establish that changing dietary precursor or cofactor intake changes brain noradrenaline firing or attention.

dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Human intake-to-noradrenaline responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the cited dopamine-metabolite and developmental evidence is not a noradrenaline-dosing trial.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Direct-section admission conflicts with the explicit limitation excluding dietary PLP provision. B6 precursor supply remains a separate accepted relationship.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Cofactor for aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase conversion of L-DOPA toward dopamine, the immediate precursor of noradrenaline
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Kennedy reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis; this does not establish dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-noradrenaline response in humans.

dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Dietary B6 can supply PLP precursors, including vitamers that enter the central nervous system, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain noradrenaline synthesis.

dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Required metal cofactor of dopamine β-hydroxylase in the conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Copper is required by the enzyme. Genetic copper-trafficking disease and animal deficiency models are not evidence that extra dietary copper raises brain noradrenaline when copper status is adequate.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Electron donor that keeps the copper sites of dopamine β-hydroxylase reduced so dopamine can be hydroxylated to noradrenaline
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Ascorbate is required in the reaction. That does not show that ordinary dietary vitamin C increases human brain noradrenaline or improves attention when vitamin C status is adequate.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: The reviewed LNAA pool presents tyrosine through [BRS1 PM2 — LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) for synthesis of dopamine, the immediate precursor converted by DBH into noradrenaline.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Tyrosine is upstream precursor supply, not the immediate DBH substrate or an independently adjudicated Direct dietary requirement here. Ordinary dietary competitive changes do not establish a limiting effect on regional noradrenergic signalling or benefit from extra tyrosine.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Folate supplies the methyl group through [BRS2 PM1 — Folate/B12 remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation), replenishing methionine used by [BRS2 PM3 — MAT/SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is the methyl donor used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: This requires functional B12-dependent remethylation. The connected reaction chain does not measure dietary folate contribution to regional brain SAM or clearance; alternative methionine supply and tissue turnover matter. A limiting effect and benefit from extra intake remain unresolved.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Betaine donates methyl groups through [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: This is peripheral BHMT supply, not neuronal BHMT activity or measured delivery into neural SAM. Dietary methionine and folate remethylation provide alternatives. Homocysteine lowering does not establish regional clearance, a limiting constraint or benefit from extra intake.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Choline can be oxidised to betaine for [BRS2 PM2 — BHMT remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation), predominantly in liver and kidney, replenishing methionine upstream of [BRS2 PM3 — SAM synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis). SAM is used by COMT during noradrenaline metabolism.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Only choline-to-betaine methyl supply is admitted, not membrane or acetylcholine roles. Oxidation, peripheral BHMT, alternative methionine supply and local neural SAM turnover limit interpretation. Neural delivery, increased clearance, a limiting constraint and extra-intake benefit are not measured.

dietary_input_traceability.dietary_input_note: Accepted dietary provision or constituent supply relationship; no efficacy or quantity claim added.
dietary_input_traceability.biological_role: Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of noradrenaline synthesis.
dietary_input_traceability.evidence_limitation: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: Iron is a Direct cofactor requirement for tyrosine hydroxylase. This does not establish that additional iron increases brain noradrenaline when iron status is adequate.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Human intake-to-noradrenaline responsiveness and clinical benefit were not established; the cited dopamine-metabolite and developmental evidence is not a noradrenaline-dosing trial.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: PLP is the Direct cofactor requirement for aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase on the catecholamine path to noradrenaline. This does not establish dietary PLP provision.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Kennedy reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis; this does not establish dietary PLP provision or an intake-to-noradrenaline response in humans.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: Vitamin B6 is a Derived Dietary Requirement because dietary B6 vitamers are converted to PLP. This does not establish that increasing B6 intake increases noradrenaline synthesis or improves attention.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Dietary B6 can supply PLP precursors, including vitamers that enter the central nervous system, but increasing B6 intake has not been shown to increase human brain noradrenaline synthesis.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: Copper is a Direct cofactor requirement of dopamine β-hydroxylase. This does not establish that additional copper increases brain noradrenaline when copper status is adequate.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Copper is required by the enzyme. Genetic copper-trafficking disease and animal deficiency models are not evidence that extra dietary copper raises brain noradrenaline when copper status is adequate.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: Vitamin C (ascorbate) is a Direct cofactor requirement of dopamine β-hydroxylase as the electron donor. This does not establish that additional vitamin C increases brain noradrenaline or improves attention when vitamin C status is adequate.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Ascorbate is required in the reaction. That does not show that ordinary dietary vitamin C increases human brain noradrenaline or improves attention when vitamin C status is adequate.

dietary_lever_atoms.permitted_wording: Phenylalanine is hydroxylated to tyrosine in peripheral tissues, replenishing the circulating tyrosine available to [LAT1 transport](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) upstream of noradrenaline synthesis.
dietary_lever_atoms.evidence_limitation: Human peripheral conversion supplies circulating tyrosine; neuronal delivery uses the separately supported transport chain. This does not establish increased dopamine/noradrenaline output, a limiting intake or benefit from extra phenylalanine. Hydroxylation, renal/hepatic function and LNAA competition matter; high phenylalanine is not interchangeable with tyrosine.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Copper
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Copper is the metal that dopamine β-hydroxylase needs in order to convert dopamine into noradrenaline. Brain copper is tightly controlled and is not the same as a serum copper reading.

dietary_lever_presentations.label: Vitamin C (ascorbate)
dietary_lever_presentations.reader_description: Vitamin C (ascorbate) donates electrons that keep the copper sites of dopamine β-hydroxylase in the reduced form needed for that conversion. Humans must obtain vitamin C from the diet; that is not a rule to take extra vitamin C to raise noradrenaline.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Noradrenaline helps set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged {{cite:odonnell_norepinephrine_2012}}. That biological role is not a dietary-treatment claim, and ADHD imaging that varies by dopamine process does not show a uniform noradrenaline deficit or a food-based attention effect {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

Noradrenaline can change arousal and effort-related tone, but dopaminergic reward circuitry remains the primary biological driver of Motivation / Drive {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}. The attached sources do not measure motivation after a dietary change, and iron-deficiency reviews are not motivation trials {{cite:beard_iron_2003}}.

Catecholamine systems can sit near reward and incentive-motivation biology, but the attached insulin–dopamine review does not measure noradrenaline signalling or a pleasure outcome after diet {{cite:gruber_impact_2023}}. Dopamine-process heterogeneity in ADHD is not a pleasure-capacity finding for this mechanism {{cite:macdonald_dopamine_2024}}.

candidate_cross_brs_relationships.relationship_scope: One-carbon metabolism and SAM-dependent COMT activity against catecholamines

scientific_findings.finding_label: Noradrenaline supports arousal, vigilance and executive control
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine) is a neuromodulator that changes how many brain-cell types respond, helping set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged. That is a signalling role, not a dietary dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports the mechanism’s attention and arousal mission. It does not show that changing food intake raises brain noradrenaline or treats ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Noradrenaline modulates arousal, vigilance and executive-control processes by changing the gain of multiple central-nervous-system cell types rather than acting as a single directional attention chemical.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The attached review treats norepinephrine as a widespread neuromodulator that optimises central-nervous-system performance by acting on several cell types. That account matches the mission of supporting alertness and executive control. It does not measure dietary intake, brain noradrenaline after meals, or a clinical attention outcome.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The source is a mechanistic review, not a human dietary or ADHD trial. It does not isolate receptor subtypes, quantify everyday noradrenaline tone, or show that precursor or cofactor intake changes signalling.

evidence_considered.label: O'Donnell et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Norepinephrine acts as a neuromodulator across multiple central-nervous-system cell types to support optimised performance, including arousal and vigilance-related functions.

assessment.study: Narrative review of norepinephrine as a multi-cell-type neuromodulator.
assessment.population: Mixed experimental and human mechanistic literature; not a dietary intervention sample.
assessment.result: Identified norepinephrine as a gain-setting neuromodulator rather than a single-target attention chemical.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled functional or dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the signalling role this mechanism represents.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; does not demonstrate dietary modification or a clinical attention benefit.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Noradrenaline formation shares catecholamine synthesis requirements
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Noradrenaline is formed from dopamine on the tyrosine-derived catecholamine path. Iron supports tyrosine hydroxylase, and pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP; the active form of vitamin B6) supports decarboxylation toward dopamine. These shared steps are biological requirements, not proof that extra iron or B6 raises brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Tyrosine remains the pathway starting material. Circulating amino-acid supply, competitive brain entry and dopamine formation are earlier steps. The later conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline is assessed in the dopamine β-hydroxylase finding.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Noradrenaline formation depends on the shared tyrosine-to-dopamine catecholamine sequence, including iron- and PLP-dependent enzyme steps; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Iron-deficiency review evidence identifies iron as required for tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step from tyrosine toward dopamine and then noradrenaline. B-vitamin review evidence places PLP in neurochemical decarboxylation, and a transport study shows that B6 vitamers can enter the central nervous system. Together they support shared pathway dependence. They do not show ordinary-diet control of human brain noradrenaline. The later dopamine β-hydroxylase step is assessed separately.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The most direct deficiency discussion is preclinical or developmental. The sources do not establish common inadequacy in a defined clinical population, responsiveness when status is already adequate, or an attention benefit mediated by noradrenaline.

evidence_considered.label: Beard et al. (2003)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Iron deficiency alters developing-brain catecholamine biology, including tyrosine-hydroxylase-dependent synthesis toward dopamine and noradrenaline.

assessment.study: Narrative review of iron deficiency, brain development and neurotransmitter systems.
assessment.population: Mixed human developmental and experimental-animal literature.
assessment.result: Identified iron as required for tyrosine hydroxylase and described catecholamine-system sensitivity under deficiency.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No human intake-to-noradrenaline effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports iron as a shared catecholamine-synthesis cofactor relevant to noradrenaline formation.
assessment.limitations: Predominantly deficiency and developmental evidence; not a human noradrenaline-dosing or attention trial.

evidence_dependency: The later dopamine-to-noradrenaline conversion is assessed in PM4-F4 rather than restated here.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Kennedy (2016)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews B-vitamin roles in neurochemical synthesis, including vitamin B6 as cofactor context for catecholamine formation.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: General B-vitamin review; it does not isolate aromatic L-amino-acid decarboxylase or show an intake-to-noradrenaline response.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Spector (1978)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Shows that B6 vitamers enter the central nervous system and contribute to the brain vitamin B6 pool.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Rabbit transport study; it does not measure noradrenaline synthesis, release or function.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Dopamine β-hydroxylase converts dopamine to noradrenaline using copper and ascorbate
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Dopamine β-hydroxylase hydroxylates dopamine to noradrenaline inside vesicles. The enzyme needs copper at its active sites and ascorbate as the electron donor that keeps that copper reduced. These are reaction requirements, not proof that extra dietary copper or vitamin C raises brain noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This finding identifies copper and vitamin C (ascorbate) as candidates for dietary assessment. It does not admit an intake-responsive noradrenaline lever or an attention benefit.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Conversion of dopamine to noradrenaline by dopamine β-hydroxylase requires enzyme-bound copper and ascorbate as the electron donor; those biochemical requirements are not evidence of intake-responsive human brain noradrenaline or a functional benefit.
scientific_findings.synthesis: A 2026 catecholamine review identifies dopamine β-hydroxylase as a copper-dependent monooxygenase that uses molecular oxygen and ascorbate to form noradrenaline, and states that this is the only catecholamine-synthesis step with a direct mechanistic ascorbate requirement. The human crystal structure shows two copper ions per subunit and two ascorbate-derived electrons per turnover. Brain-copper and brain-ascorbate reviews place the same cuproenzyme and reductant in central-nervous-system catecholamine chemistry, while noting that circulating copper is not brain copper. Together they establish the defining conversion and its participants. Genetic copper-trafficking disease, animal copper deficiency and high-dose intravenous vitamin C in septic shock are not ordinary-diet evidence.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The synthesis is mechanistic and review-level. It does not show that ordinary dietary copper or vitamin C changes human brain noradrenaline, attention or ADHD when status is already adequate.

evidence_considered.label: Goldstein and Eisenhofer (2026)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dopamine β-hydroxylase converts dopamine to noradrenaline and requires copper, molecular oxygen and ascorbate as the electron donor that keeps active-site copper reduced.

assessment.study: Integrative review of catecholamine synthesis, storage, release, reuptake and metabolism.
assessment.population: Mixed human physiological, clinical-pathophysiological and experimental literature; not a dietary trial sample.
assessment.result: Identified copper and ascorbate as required participants in the dopamine-to-noradrenaline step and noted that this is the only catecholamine step with a direct ascorbate requirement.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or functional effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the defining conversion and its cofactor chemistry.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; disease and kinetic examples are not ordinary-diet interventions.

evidence_considered.label: Vendelboe et al. (2016)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human dopamine β-hydroxylase requires two copper ions per subunit and two ascorbate-derived electrons for hydroxylation of dopamine.

assessment.study: Crystal structure of human dopamine β-hydroxylase at 2.9 Å.
assessment.population: Structural biochemistry; not a human dietary sample.
assessment.result: Confirmed two type-2 copper sites per subunit and ascorbate dependence of the monooxygenase class.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Structural, not a dose-response estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independently supports copper and ascorbate as reaction participants.
assessment.limitations: Isolated-protein structure; does not measure diet, brain noradrenaline or function.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Scheiber, Mercer and Dringen (2014)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews copper functions in brain, including dopamine β-hydroxylase, and distinguishes tightly regulated brain copper from circulating measures.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Brain-copper review; it does not isolate a dietary copper-to-noradrenaline trial.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Lutsenko et al. (2019)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews copper and the brain noradrenergic system, including Menkes copper-trafficking disease and animal dietary-deficiency effects on catecholamines.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Disease and animal-deficiency evidence; not ordinary-diet modulation in copper-replete humans.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Harrison and May (2009)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews high brain ascorbate and SVCT2 transport, including a role as reductant for dopamine β-hydroxylase.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Transport and compartmentation review; it does not show that extra dietary vitamin C raises human brain noradrenaline.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Attention relevance is not a dietary or ADHD-treatment finding
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The attached sources support noradrenaline as attention-relevant biology. They do not show that meals, iron or B6 change human noradrenaline signalling, and they do not show a uniform ADHD lesion that diet can correct.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Keep biological relevance separate from dietary modulation and from dopamine-process findings that are not noradrenaline measurements.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Repository evidence supports a translational relationship from noradrenergic signalling to Focus / Attention Stability without establishing dietary modification of noradrenaline or an ADHD treatment effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis: O’Donnell supplies the neuromodulatory attention and arousal account. MacDonald shows that ADHD-related catecholamine findings vary by process and method and cannot be restated as a single deficit. Fernstrom describes meal-level precursor transport upstream of signalling. Together they support a biology-to-attention mapping while blocking a food-as-noradrenaline-treatment reading.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: No attached study measures attention after a dietary change aimed at noradrenaline. Plasma amino-acid ratios and dopamine-process reviews are not noradrenaline signalling.

evidence_considered.label: O'Donnell et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Norepinephrine neuromodulation is relevant to central-nervous-system performance including arousal and vigilance, without testing diet or ADHD treatment.

assessment.study: Same mechanistic review used for PM4-F1, reused here for the attention-relationship proposition.
assessment.population: Mixed mechanistic literature; not a dietary or ADHD-outcome sample.
assessment.result: Supports attention-relevant signalling biology without a treatment or intake effect.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No clinical or dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the Phenome mapping in signalling biology.
assessment.limitations: Review; no dietary or ADHD endpoint.

evidence_considered.label: MacDonald et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: ADHD-related dopamine findings are heterogeneous across process, region and method and do not support a uniform global deficit that can be treated as a noradrenaline-diet claim.

assessment.study: Critical review of the dopamine hypothesis in ADHD.
assessment.population: Children and adults with ADHD, comparison groups and relevant animal models.
assessment.result: Reported mixed dopamine-related findings rather than one directional lesion.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled noradrenaline or dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Constrains ADHD wording attached to this Phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: Dopamine-focused; not a noradrenaline dietary trial.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Fernstrom (2013)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Describes meal-level large-neutral-amino-acid transport that can change tyrosine presentation before catecholamine synthesis.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Transport and plasma-ratio biology; it does not measure noradrenaline signalling or attention.

evidence_dependency: O'Donnell et al. (2012) is also primary evidence in PM4-F1. Reuse here answers the Phenome-relationship proposition, not an independent replication of the signalling review.
Fernstrom (2013) is connected evidence here and primary evidence in PM4-IC1. That is one transport review used for two propositions, not two independent studies.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Precursor transport and dopamine-process measures are not noradrenaline signalling
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Plasma amino-acid ratios, dopamine-process imaging and insulin–dopamine reviews can sit next to this mechanism. They do not measure noradrenaline release, receptor signalling or an attention outcome of changing diet.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Use these sources to keep measurements distinct. Do not promote them as headline noradrenaline Findings.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: LAT1-related precursor presentation, heterogeneous dopamine-process measures and insulin–dopamine reward reviews are not interchangeable with noradrenergic signalling.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Fernstrom addresses competitive precursor transport. MacDonald addresses dopamine processes in ADHD. Gruber reviews insulin and dopamine in reward disruption. Each is useful as a boundary on how other evidence is read. None establishes noradrenaline signalling change or a dietary attention effect.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Interpretive only. These sources do not fill the missing human dietary-to-noradrenaline measurement.
evidence_dependency: Fernstrom (2013) is also connected evidence in PM4-F3. Reuse here constrains measurement identity, not a second transport experiment.
Fernstrom (2013) is also reused in PM4-F7 for precursor presentation; this is not independent replication.

evidence_considered.label: Fernstrom (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Dietary and plasma large-neutral-amino-acid ratios influence brain precursor presentation; that is transport biology, not measured noradrenaline signalling.

assessment.study: Narrative review of dietary large-neutral-amino-acid effects on brain transport and neurochemistry.
assessment.population: Mixed human and experimental literature.
assessment.result: Identified competitive transport as a determinant of precursor entry.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No noradrenaline or attention effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Constrains reading meal-amino-acid evidence as noradrenaline signalling.
assessment.limitations: Review; no noradrenaline endpoint.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Gruber et al. (2023)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews insulin and dopamine in reward disruption, which is sometimes cited next to catecholamine supply.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Insulin–dopamine framing; it does not measure noradrenaline or a pleasure outcome of diet on this mechanism.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Regional clearance and receptor actions connect noradrenaline with dopamine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Prefrontal catecholamine regulation includes receptor-dependent actions and shared regional clearance, rather than separate linear precursor-to-transmitter pathways.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Noradrenergic regulation extends beyond precursor supply. These experiments do not establish nutritional modulation or a clinical treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Prefrontal catecholamine regulation includes receptor-dependent actions and shared regional clearance, rather than separate linear precursor-to-transmitter pathways.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Monkey pharmacological experiments implicate alpha2-adrenergic and D1 receptors in prefrontal regulation. Mouse uptake experiments establish a regional NET contribution to dopamine clearance. The studies test different links, not one replicated protocol.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Animal experiments; no nutrient manipulation, human ADHD outcome or universal transporter rule.

evidence_considered.label: Gamo, Wang and Arnsten (2010)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Moderate drug doses improved performance; alpha2 or D1 blockade prevented improvement, and neuronal effects were dose-dependent.

assessment.study: Monkey delayed-response behaviour and prefrontal neuronal recordings with pharmacological receptor blockade.
assessment.population: Monkeys; pharmacological experiments.
assessment.result: Moderate drug doses improved performance; alpha2 or D1 blockade prevented improvement, and neuronal effects were dose-dependent.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Context-specific experimental result; no dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Moderate drug doses improved performance; alpha2 or D1 blockade prevented improvement, and neuronal effects were dose-dependent.
assessment.limitations: Animal pharmacology; no dietary exposure or human ADHD endpoint.

evidence_considered.label: Morón et al. (2002)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Frontal-cortex dopamine uptake depended primarily on NET; caudate and accumbens uptake depended primarily on DAT.

assessment.study: Radiolabelled dopamine uptake in regional synaptosomes using transporter inhibitors and knockout mice.
assessment.population: Wild-type and NET/DAT knockout mice.
assessment.result: Frontal-cortex dopamine uptake depended primarily on NET; caudate and accumbens uptake depended primarily on DAT.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Context-specific experimental result; no dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Frontal-cortex dopamine uptake depended primarily on NET; caudate and accumbens uptake depended primarily on DAT.
assessment.limitations: Ex vivo mouse uptake; developmental knockout effects and regional differences limit generalisation.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Locus-coeruleus firing tracks attended cues
scientific_findings.finding_summary: In a monkey vigilance task, locus-coeruleus neurons showed target-linked phasic activity that varied with performance.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Noradrenergic regulation extends beyond precursor supply. These experiments do not establish nutritional modulation or a clinical treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: In a monkey vigilance task, locus-coeruleus neurons showed target-linked phasic activity that varied with performance.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Neuronal recordings support firing-pattern regulation as distinct from substrate provision. They do not establish that changing precursor intake changes firing or performance.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Association in four monkeys; no causal intervention or ordinary-diet inference.

evidence_considered.label: Aston-Jones et al. (1994)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Target-linked phasic responses weakened during poorer task performance.

assessment.study: Extracellular locus-coeruleus recordings during an oddball vigilance task.
assessment.population: Four cynomolgus monkeys.
assessment.result: Target-linked phasic responses weakened during poorer task performance.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Context-specific experimental result; no dietary effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Target-linked phasic responses weakened during poorer task performance.
assessment.limitations: Observational neuronal/task association; no manipulation proving causation and no dietary or ADHD trial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Remethylation supplies the methionine/SAM resource used by COMT
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Remethylation can replenish methionine for SAM synthesis; human COMT uses SAM to methylate noradrenaline.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This establishes the connected biochemical supply route, not a measured dietary effect on regional neural SAM or COMT clearance. BHMT is predominantly hepatic/renal; peripheral methionine contribution, local SAM synthesis, alternative supply and turnover vary by tissue. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint and benefit from extra intake in replete individuals remain unresolved.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Verified BRS2 PM1/PM2/PM3 Findings establish folate-dependent remethylation, betaine/BHMT remethylation, choline-to-betaine provision and MAT substrate use. Lotta's recombinant human COMT work establishes the downstream methyl-transfer reaction. These successive reactions support upstream resource provision. They do not directly measure transfer of a dietary donor into regional neural SAM or a change in signalling.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This establishes the connected biochemical supply route, not a measured dietary effect on regional neural SAM or COMT clearance. BHMT is predominantly hepatic/renal; peripheral methionine contribution, local SAM synthesis, alternative supply and turnover vary by tissue. Donor inadequacy as a limiting constraint and benefit from extra intake in replete individuals remain unresolved.

evidence_considered.label: Froese et al. (2019)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes folate/B12 remethylation and placement before MAT synthesis; reviewed on PM1-F1.

evidence_considered.label: Obeid (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes betaine donation and choline provision in connected remethylation; reviewed on PM2-F1/F2.

evidence_considered.label: Bailey et al. (2021)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Establishes methionine and ATP use in human MAT2A; reviewed on PM3-F1.

evidence_considered.label: Evans et al. (2002)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human BHMT reaction identity; supports betaine-to-methionine provision, not dietary MAT responsiveness.

evidence_considered.label: Salvi and Gadda (2013)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Choline oxidation through betaine aldehyde to betaine; supports route identity, not MAT flux.

evidence_considered.label: Lotta et al. (1995)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Recombinant human COMT catalysed SAM-dependent methylation of dopamine and noradrenaline.

assessment.study: Kinetic characterisation of recombinant soluble and membrane-bound human COMT.
assessment.population: Human proteins expressed in bacterial and insect-cell systems; not a dietary or in-vivo neural trial.

## BRS1-1-4 - Noradrenergic Signalling (Attention & Executive Modulation) ## 1. Mission & Overview ### Mission Support noradrenergic alertness and executive control so attention and arousal stay appropriately engaged. **Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Supported
- Iron - Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor) - Vitamin B6 - Copper - Vitamin C (ascorbate)
- Iron - Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor)
- Monoamine precursor supply **Individual KC inputs** - Tyrosine - Phenylalanine - Methyl-resource supply for COMT **Individual KC inputs** - Vitamin B9 (folate) - Betaine - Choline
### Overview Noradrenaline, also called norepinephrine, helps set arousal, vigilance and executive control so attention can stay engaged. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Neurons make it from dopamine, then shape the signal through release, receptors, reuptake and breakdown. [[9]](#pm-ref-9) [[10]](#pm-ref-10) This coordination lets alertness follow cognitive demand. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Iron, vitamin B6, copper and vitamin C take part in that chemistry. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) [[13]](#pm-ref-13) - **Benefits:** Noradrenaline helps keep arousal and vigilance matched to cognitive demand. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) - **Implementation Notes:** Iron, vitamin B6, copper, and vitamin C are the cofactors on the path from dopamine to noradrenaline. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[7]](#pm-ref-7) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) [[13]](#pm-ref-13) Extra intake when status is already adequate is not established to raise brain noradrenaline or improve attention. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) - **Biological Relevance:** This tunes alert engagement rather than creating the precursor pool. [[2]](#pm-ref-2) ## 2. Primary Biological Effects ↑ norepinephrine signalling; ↑ attention; ↑ executive modulation ## 3. Intervention Levers

Only categories with a substantive evidence-qualified intervention are shown.

No evidence-qualified lifestyle relationship is projected. Exercise is not a Dietary Requirement of noradrenergic signalling.
## 4. Mechanistic Basis ### Summary Noradrenergic signalling relevant to attention, arousal and executive control depends on the tyrosine-derived catecholamine path and on cofactor context described under [BRS1(FM1) — Monoaminergic Function](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-monoaminergic-function). Physical activity, sleep and stress can also shape catecholamine tone; those relationships are not established here as dietary requirements.
#### (Noradrenergic pathways and attention) Norepinephrine modulates attention, arousal, and executive processes frequently impaired in attention-related conditions. Alterations in noradrenergic signalling have been associated with differences in attention regulation and response inhibition → [O'Donnell et al., 2012] #### (Firing, receptor actions and regional clearance) Noradrenergic signalling depends on when neurons fire, which receptors respond and how transmitters are cleared. Monkey pharmacology supports alpha2-adrenergic and D1 contributions to prefrontal regulation Gamo, Wang and Arnsten (2010) [[16]](#pm-ref-16). Mouse experiments identify NET-mediated dopamine uptake in frontal cortex Morón et al. (2002) [[17]](#pm-ref-17). Locus-coeruleus recordings link phasic responses to attended cues Aston-Jones et al. (1994) [[18]](#pm-ref-18). These distinct experimental links support regulated signalling beyond synthesis; they do not establish dietary control or human ADHD benefit. #### (Precursor and cofactor dependence) Noradrenaline is formed from dopamine on the tyrosine-derived catecholamine path. Circulating tyrosine comes from the amino-acid pool described by [BRS1-FM1-PM1 — Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm1-amino-acid-availability-and-prioritisation). Meal-level large-neutral-amino-acid transport is described by [BRS1-FM1-PM2 — LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) and Fernstrom (2013) [[2]](#pm-ref-2). Iron is required by tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step from tyrosine toward dopamine and then noradrenaline Beard et al. (2003) [[3]](#pm-ref-3). Dopamine β-hydroxylase then converts dopamine to noradrenaline and requires copper and ascorbate Goldstein and Eisenhofer (2026) [[9]](#pm-ref-9). #### (Diet-supported rather than diet-dominant) Meal-level substrate and cofactor supply sit beside physical activity, sleep and stress context. Those lifestyle relationships are not established here as dietary requirements. #### (Cross-system context) Catecholamine inactivation can involve COMT, which uses SAM from one-carbon metabolism. The attached corpus does not establish that methylation-cycle diet changes noradrenaline signalling. Glycaemic volatility can change arousal indirectly; that is not a noradrenaline dietary finding. Together this mechanism extends catecholamine coverage from dopamine formation to noradrenergic attention and executive modulation.
### 4.1 Scientific Findings #### Summary Structural and biochemical evidence establishes copper and ascorbate participation in the defining dopamine-to-noradrenaline conversion. [[10]](#pm-ref-10) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) Animal pharmacology and neuronal recordings separately support receptor-dependent prefrontal regulation and firing-pattern responses to attended cues. [[16]](#pm-ref-16) [[18]](#pm-ref-18) These findings support distinct synthesis and signalling processes; they do not establish that changing dietary precursor or cofactor intake changes brain noradrenaline firing or attention. ## 5. BRS Pathways and Connections ### 5.1 BRS Pathways [BRS1-FM1-PM1 — Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm1-amino-acid-availability-and-prioritisation) ↓ [BRS1-FM1-PM2 — LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) ↓ [BRS1-FM1-PM3 — Dopaminergic Signalling Regulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm3-dopaminergic-signalling-regulation) ↓ [BRS1-FM1-PM4 — Noradrenergic Signalling](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm4-noradrenergic-signalling-attention-executive-modulation) [BRS1-FM1-PM1 — Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm1-amino-acid-availability-and-prioritisation) ↓ [BRS1-FM1-PM2 — LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) ↓ [BRS1-FM1-PM5 — Serotonergic Signalling Regulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm5-serotonergic-signalling-regulation) ### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships Primary Mechanisms in other Biological Regulatory Systems that directly interact with, constrain or support this mechanism. - [BRS2(FM1) — Methylation Cycle Efficiency](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-methylation-cycle-efficiency) — Catecholamine inactivation can use COMT, which depends on SAM from one-carbon metabolism. The attached corpus does not establish that ordinary methylation-cycle variation controls noradrenaline signalling or attention. ### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function. - [BRS1-FM1-PM1 - Amino-Acid Availability & Prioritisation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm1-amino-acid-availability-and-prioritisation) — Supplies the circulating amino-acid pool, including tyrosine used on the catecholamine path to noradrenaline. Amino-acid quality and precursor-pool adequacy are assessed there. That is precursor supply, not noradrenaline signalling. - [BRS1-FM1-PM2 - LAT1 Competitive Transport Modulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm2-lat1-competitive-transport-modulation) — Governs competitive brain entry of large neutral amino acids, including tyrosine, after a meal. Transport bias is not noradrenaline synthesis or receptor signalling. - [BRS1-FM1-PM3 - Dopaminergic Signalling Regulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm3-dopaminergic-signalling-regulation) — Forms dopamine, the immediate precursor converted to noradrenaline, and shares the tyrosine-hydroxylase and decarboxylase steps. Dopaminergic signalling is not noradrenergic signalling. - [BRS1-FM1-PM5 - Serotonergic Signalling Regulation](/docs/biological-targets/brs1/fm1/brs1-fm1-pm5-serotonergic-signalling-regulation) — Parallel monoamine path from shared precursor transport. It does not feed noradrenaline synthesis. ## 7. Phenome Connections These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

Each Phenome relationship has two independent ratings. They are not combined or averaged.

Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength

How direct and important is this biological mechanism expected to be to the Phenome within the BRAIN model?

Evidence Confidence

How strongly does the adjudicated evidence support this particular biology → Phenome relationship?

Focus / Attention Stability — modulates Open Page → →
- **Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength:** High - **Evidence Confidence:** Low–Medium - **Rationale:** Noradrenaline helps set arousal and vigilance so attention and executive control can stay engaged O'Donnell et al. (2012) [[1]](#pm-ref-1). That biological role is not a dietary-treatment claim, and ADHD imaging that varies by dopamine process does not show a uniform noradrenaline deficit or a food-based attention effect MacDonald et al. (2024) [[4]](#pm-ref-4). **Supporting evidence**
Motivation / Drive — modulates Open Page → →
- **Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength:** Medium - **Evidence Confidence:** Low–Medium - **Rationale:** Noradrenaline can change arousal and effort-related tone, but dopaminergic reward circuitry remains the primary biological driver of Motivation / Drive MacDonald et al. title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.
rationale: Tryptophan provision, LAT1 competition, TPH2 flux and serotonin signalling are separate. Current corpus includes bibliographic gaps; no unverified serotonin food claim exported.

data.title: Serotonergic Signalling Regulation
data.mission: Support serotonergic signalling so mood stability, inhibition, and behavioural regulation remain well grounded.
data.summary: Serotonin is made in neurons when tryptophan is converted through two enzyme steps, then shaped by release, receptors, reuptake and breakdown. Across brain regions, the same transmitter can support different responses. That system supports mood stability, inhibition and behavioural regulation. Tryptophan, iron and vitamin B6 are part of the chemistry.
data.dose_sensitivity: No intake-response range established; serotonin effects are receptor-, region- and task-dependent

pm_kc_relationships.pm_biological_role: Ordinary LAT1 large-neutral-amino-acid imbalance can constrain serotonin-formation capacity. The public sentence states that biology without a mood or ADHD claim. KC food lists are not inherited.
pm_kc_relationships.evidence_limitation: The mapping is constrained-by synthesis capacity. It does not establish serotonin release, receptor signalling, mood change, or a Dietary Requirement.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Serotonin signalling is a core biological substrate for emotional regulation, impulse control and affective stability {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. ADHD-focused serotonin reviews do not establish a uniform serotonin deficit that diet can correct {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}} {{cite:banerjee_does_2015}}.

Serotonin signalling participates in emotional processing and stress-related control {{cite:shaw_emotion_2014}}. The attached sources do not measure stress resilience after a dietary change aimed at serotonin {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.
Serotonin participates in sleep–wake and calming neurochemistry {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Meal-level precursor transport is not a sleep outcome {{cite:fernstrom_lnna_2013}}.

Serotonin can interact with dopaminergic reward circuits and behavioural inhibition {{cite:faraone_serotonin_2025}}. That interaction is not a measured reward outcome after diet {{cite:tang_nutritional_2025}}.

Serotonin signalling intersects negative-valence and control circuits discussed in mood and anxiety contexts {{cite:briguglio_dietary_2018}}. Systemic-inflammation connectivity is not a serotonin measurement {{cite:marsland_systemic_2017}}.

Serotonin pathways sit near positive-valence mood biology {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. Saffron supplementation trials are not serotonin-process measurements and are not a Dietary Requirement of this mechanism {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

Serotonin can modulate affiliative and social-affective behaviour in translational accounts {{cite:berger_serotonin_2009}}. A saffron social-relationship outcome is not a serotonin signalling measurement {{cite:jackson_effects_2021}}.

data.scientific_findings_intro: Enzyme studies and biochemical reviews establish the neuronal tryptophan-to-serotonin synthesis sequence and its cofactor dependence. [[13]](#pm-ref-13) [[14]](#pm-ref-14) [[12]](#pm-ref-12) Broader reviews support receptor diversity and transporter-mediated handling as additional determinants of serotonergic function. [[15]](#pm-ref-15) Together, the evidence supports synthesis and signalling as related but distinct capacities; it does not directly establish that ordinary dietary changes regulate human brain serotonin or produce uniform functional benefits.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Serotonin supports mood stability, inhibition and behavioural regulation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is a neuromodulator that helps set emotional tone, behavioural inhibition and related control. That is a signalling role, not a dietary dosing rule.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: This supports the mechanism’s mood-stability and inhibition mission. It does not show that changing food intake raises brain serotonin or treats mood, sleep or ADHD.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Serotonin modulates emotional processing, impulse control and behavioural regulation rather than acting as a single directional mood chemical.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Human emotion-dysregulation and ADHD-related serotonin reviews treat serotonergic signalling as relevant to affective stability and inhibition. A broader serotonin-biology review places the same transmitter across receptor families that shape mood- and behaviour-related circuits. Together they support the signalling mission. They do not measure dietary intake, brain serotonin after meals, or a uniform clinical lesion that food can correct.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The sources are reviews, not dietary trials. They do not isolate everyday serotonin tone, quantify receptor-specific effects after meals, or show that precursor or cofactor intake changes signalling.

evidence_considered.directional_finding: Emotion dysregulation in ADHD is discussed as a clinically important phenotype with serotonergic and broader monoamine context, without testing diet.

assessment.study: Narrative review of emotion dysregulation in ADHD.
assessment.population: Children and adults with ADHD and comparison groups described in the reviewed literature.
assessment.result: Identified emotion dysregulation as a core associated feature rather than a single-chemical deficit.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No pooled dietary or serotonin-process effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Anchors the mood-stability and inhibition mission in human clinical-mechanistic literature.
assessment.limitations: ADHD-focused review; not a serotonin dietary trial.

evidence_considered.label: Berger, Gray and Roth (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Serotonin acts through multiple receptor families and central circuits that include mood, sleep–wake and behavioural-control functions.

assessment.study: Narrative review of expanded serotonin biology.
assessment.population: Mixed experimental and human mechanistic literature; not a dietary sample.
assessment.result: Described receptor diversity and non-dietary physiological roles of serotonin.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or clinical effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes serotonin as a multi-receptor neuromodulator rather than a single mood chemical.
assessment.limitations: Review synthesis; does not demonstrate dietary modification.

connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Hypothesis review; not a dietary or process-specific measurement.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Serotonin formation depends on tryptophan hydroxylation and PLP-dependent decarboxylation
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Brain serotonin is formed from tryptophan. Tryptophan hydroxylase (the first and rate-limiting enzyme) needs iron and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Pyridoxal-5′-phosphate (PLP; the active form of vitamin B6) then supports decarboxylation of 5-hydroxytryptophan to serotonin. These are biological requirements, not proof that extra tryptophan, iron or B6 raises brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Tryptophan remains the pathway starting material. Circulating amino-acid supply and competitive brain entry are earlier steps. Iron, BH4 and PLP are candidates for dietary assessment. This finding does not admit an intake-responsive serotonin lever.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Serotonin formation depends on tryptophan-hydroxylase conversion of tryptophan to 5-hydroxytryptophan, requiring iron and BH4, followed by PLP-dependent decarboxylation; cofactor or substrate necessity is not evidence of intake-responsive human brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Aromatic-amino-acid hydroxylase biochemistry identifies tryptophan hydroxylase as an iron- and tetrahydrobiopterin-dependent monooxygenase that forms 5-hydroxytryptophan. A second tryptophan hydroxylase isoform (TPH2) accounts for neuronal serotonin synthesis. BH4-pathway review evidence places the same cofactor on serotonin as well as dopamine synthesis. B-vitamin review evidence places PLP in neurochemical decarboxylation, and a transport study shows that B6 vitamers can enter the central nervous system. Together they establish the defining synthesis sequence and its participants. They do not show ordinary-diet control of human brain serotonin.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The synthesis is mechanistic and review-level. It does not show that ordinary dietary tryptophan, iron or vitamin B6 changes human brain serotonin, mood, sleep or ADHD when status is already adequate.

evidence_considered.label: Fitzpatrick (1999)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Tryptophan hydroxylase is a tetrahydropterin-dependent aromatic amino-acid hydroxylase that uses non-haem iron and molecular oxygen to form 5-hydroxytryptophan.

assessment.population: Enzyme and experimental literature; not a human dietary sample.
assessment.result: Identified iron, tetrahydrobiopterin and oxygen as required participants in tryptophan hydroxylation.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary or functional effect estimate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Establishes the rate-limiting hydroxylation chemistry.
assessment.limitations: Enzyme-mechanism review; not an intake-to-serotonin trial.

assessment.population: Experimental biochemistry and mouse genetics; not a dietary trial.

assessment.evidence_summary: Places the hydroxylase step in neuronal serotonin formation.
