data.scientific_findings_intro: Purified and recombinant human enzyme studies establish the two transsulfuration reaction boundaries and their PLP dependence: CBS forms cystathionine, and CGL uses it to release cysteine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) [[3]](#pm-ref-3) The findings converge on biochemical pathway identity, including cysteine’s position as a product of the second step. They do not measure whole-body dietary responsiveness or glutathione synthesis, so neither increased flux from extra vitamin B6 nor downstream benefit is established by these assays. Human tracer evidence adds a physiological boundary: moderate vitamin B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling without significantly changing total transsulfuration. [[7]](#pm-ref-7)

scientific_findings.finding_label: CBS joins homocysteine and serine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human cystathionine beta-synthase uses pyridoxal 5'-phosphate to join L-homocysteine and L-serine, forming L-cystathionine. Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active form of vitamin B6 recycled from food.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Homocysteine and serine are both substrates. The cofactor requirement does not show that eating more vitamin B6 increases cystathionine formation in people.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human cystathionine beta-synthase catalyses a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine, and pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active vitamin B6 cofactor recycled from food.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Purified human enzyme kinetics and a crystal structure agree that cystathionine beta-synthase condenses L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine and that the reaction depends on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate. A cofactor review identifies that same molecule as the active form of vitamin B6, recycled from food by the salvage pathway. Together these sources define the first reaction and its cofactor. They do not measure whole-body transsulfuration flux or an intake response.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The kinetic and structural evidence uses recombinant or crystallised human enzyme, not intact human physiology. The salvage review does not assay cystathionine beta-synthase. Substrate inhibition constants and cofactor identity do not show that ordinary vitamin B6 intake sets the reaction rate.

evidence_considered.label: Belew et al. (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human cystathionine beta-synthase catalysed the pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine, with substrate inhibition by L-homocysteine.

assessment.study: Steady-state kinetics of recombinant human cystathionine beta-synthase purified from E. coli, using a continuous coupled assay for cystathionine formation.
assessment.population: Purified recombinant human enzyme; no cells, animals, or human participants.
assessment.result: The enzyme condensed L-serine and L-homocysteine to L-cystathionine. L-Homocysteine inhibited the enzyme at higher concentrations. The reverse hydrolysis of cystathionine was slower than the condensation on a specificity basis.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported Ki for L-homocysteine was 2.1 ± 0.2 mM. The abstract states that kcat/Km for cystathionine hydrolysis was approximately 2-fold lower than kcat/Km for L-serine in the condensation.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human-enzyme evidence that both serine and homocysteine are substrates and that pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is required.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro kinetics do not establish in-vivo flux, dietary responsiveness, or a phenome outcome.

evidence_considered.label: Meier et al. (2001)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The crystal structure of truncated human cystathionine beta-synthase describes a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent condensation of serine and homocysteine to cystathionine.

assessment.study: X-ray crystal structure of a truncated form of human cystathionine beta-synthase.
assessment.population: Crystallised human enzyme; no cells, animals, or human participants.
assessment.result: The structure shows a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent heme protein that catalyses condensation of serine and homocysteine to cystathionine.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No physiological effect size applies to this structure.
assessment.evidence_summary: Independent structural support for the same reaction and for pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence.
assessment.limitations: A static structure of a truncated enzyme does not measure flux, nutrient limitation, or dietary dose response.

evidence_considered.label: di Salvo et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is the active form of vitamin B6 and is recycled from food by the salvage pathway.

assessment.study: Narrative review of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate availability, salvage enzymes, and consequences of inadequate intracellular cofactor.
assessment.population: No new human cohort; review of human biochemistry and clinical cofactor disorders.
assessment.result: In humans, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate is recycled from food and from degraded enzymes by pyridoxal kinase, pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase, and phosphatases.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No transsulfuration rate or vitamin B6 intake-response figure is reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports the identity of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate as the vitamin B6 cofactor supplied from food. It does not assay this pathway.
assessment.limitations: A salvage review cannot show that vitamin B6 intake changes cystathionine beta-synthase flux.

evidence_dependency: di Salvo et al. (2012) is also used in PM5-IC1 to bound intake claims. It is not a second measurement of the condensation reaction.

scientific_findings.finding_label: CGL cleaves cystathionine and releases cysteine
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase is a pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme that cleaves L-cystathionine in the transsulfuration step that produces cysteine. Cysteine is the product of this step. Glutathione synthesis is a later pathway.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Cystathionine is the substrate and cysteine is the product. Cysteine is not a substrate of this conversion, and glutathione synthesis is not this reaction.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase requires pyridoxal 5'-phosphate and cleaves L-cystathionine in the transsulfuration step that produces cysteine.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Kinetic work on recombinant human cystathionine gamma-lyase shows gamma-lyase activity toward L-cystathionine and only marginal reactivity toward L-cysteine. A separate human-enzyme study identifies the enzyme as pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent and places it in the transsulfuration route that converts homocysteine to cysteine, with cystathionine as the assayed substrate. Cysteine is therefore the pathway product of this step, not its substrate. Neither study measures glutathione synthesis.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Both studies use recombinant human enzyme. The 2008 paper's numeric comparisons concern disease-associated mutants and a common polymorphism, not dietary intake. The abstracts establish cystathionine cleavage and the homocysteine-to-cysteine role; they were not used as a product-table for every coproduct. Glutathione synthesis remains outside this finding.

evidence_considered.label: Steegborn et al. (1999)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Recombinant human cystathionine gamma-lyase showed high gamma-lyase activity toward L-cystathionine and only marginal reactivity toward L-cysteine.

assessment.study: Cloning of human cystathionine gamma-lyase from Hep G2 RNA, bacterial expression, and steady-state kinetics with L-cystathionine.
assessment.population: Purified recombinant human enzyme; no human participants.
assessment.result: The enzyme preferred L-cystathionine as a gamma-lyase substrate. Reactivity toward L-cysteine and L-cystine was marginal, and cystathionine beta-lyase activity was not detected.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Reported Km for L-cystathionine was 0.5 mM and Vmax was 2.5 units/mg, with an optimum pH of 8.2.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct kinetic evidence that L-cystathionine is the substrate and that L-cysteine is a poor substrate of this enzyme.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro kinetics do not establish in-vivo flux or a dietary response. The abstract does not tabulate every coproduct.

evidence_considered.label: Zhu et al. (2008)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human cystathionine gamma-lyase is pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent, functions in the transsulfuration pathway that converts homocysteine to cysteine, and was assayed with cystathionine.

assessment.study: Kinetic and spectrophotometric comparison of wild-type human cystathionine gamma-lyase with pathogenic mutants and a common polymorphism.
assessment.population: Recombinant human enzyme variants; no human participants in the kinetic assays.
assessment.result: The polymorphism did not change cofactor content or the tested steady-state parameters. Pathogenic mutants had lower Vmax, lower pyridoxal 5'-phosphate content, and cystathionine Km values comparable to wild type.
assessment.effect_magnitude: T67I Vmax was about 3.5-fold lower and Q240E Vmax about 70-fold lower than wild type. Mutant pyridoxal 5'-phosphate content was about 4-fold and 80-fold lower. Wild-type Km was not stated in the abstract.
assessment.evidence_summary: Confirms pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence and cystathionine as the substrate in the homocysteine-to-cysteine pathway.
assessment.limitations: Mutant fold-changes describe rare enzyme defects, not ordinary diet. The study does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery.

evidence_dependency: Zhu et al. (2008) and Steegborn et al. (1999) are also cited by PM5-F4. That reuse is the same reaction evidence, not a recovery measurement.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cofactor dependence is not an intake or flux result
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Showing that the enzymes need pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, or that food vitamin B6 can be salvaged to that cofactor, does not measure pathway flux and does not show that vitamin B6 intake controls cysteine formation.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Circulating markers and cofactor biochemistry answer different questions. Neither is a licence to treat vitamin B6 intake as a proven controller of this conversion.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence and vitamin B6 salvage do not measure cystathionine beta-synthase or cystathionine gamma-lyase flux and do not prove that vitamin B6 intake controls transsulfuration.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The enzyme studies establish a cofactor requirement under biochemical conditions. The salvage review establishes that food vitamin B6 is recycled to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate. None of these sources reports a human tracer measurement of transsulfuration flux before and after a change in vitamin B6 intake. A cofactor requirement and a salvage route therefore cannot be read as proof that intake controls flux.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a boundary on the evidence in hand. It does not claim that a future intake study would be negative. The repository record previously used for a population association does not resolve to that study and is not part of this synthesis.

evidence_considered.label: di Salvo et al. (2012)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Food vitamin B6 is salvaged to pyridoxal 5'-phosphate; the review does not measure transsulfuration flux.

evidence_considered.label: Belew et al. (2009)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human cystathionine beta-synthase kinetics show pyridoxal 5'-phosphate dependence in purified enzyme, not a vitamin B6 intake effect.

evidence_dependency: Belew et al. (2009) and di Salvo et al. (2012) are also primary evidence in PM5-F1. Here they constrain interpretation; they are not independent replications of an intake trial.

scientific_findings.finding_label: ADHD homocysteine markers do not test this pathway or stress treatment
scientific_findings.finding_summary: A paediatric study found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 in boys with ADHD than in controls. It did not measure transsulfuration enzymes, cysteine production, stress reactivity, or a treatment effect.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Homocysteine concentration in that cohort must not be read as evidence that this conversion modulates stress reactivity or treats ADHD or stress.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed paediatric ADHD biomarker study does not show that transsulfuration modulates stress reactivity or that it treats stress or ADHD.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The study compared serum homocysteine, vitamin B12, vitamin D, ferritin, and iron in boys with ADHD and age-matched controls. Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 was lower in the ADHD group, and the authors treated homocysteine as a possible prognostic marker. The measurements are circulating biomarkers. They do not include cystathionine beta-synthase, cystathionine gamma-lyase, cystathionine, cysteine, pyridoxal 5'-phosphate, stress-reactivity scores, or an intervention.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a gap for the phenome relationship, not proof that no relationship exists. The cohort is boys only, the design is cross-sectional, and diagnosis-marker associations are not pathway flux.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Boys with ADHD had higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls. Transsulfuration enzymes, cysteine production, and stress outcomes were not measured.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarker comparison using spectrophotometry and immunoassays, with behavioural and cognitive assessments.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years; 67 with DSM-V ADHD and 66 age-matched controls.
assessment.result: Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 was lower in the ADHD group. Logistic regression treated homocysteine as a potential prognostic indicator. Vitamin D, ferritin, and iron were also measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The abstract reports significant group differences and does not provide the mean concentrations used here.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human observational evidence about serum homocysteine and vitamin B12 in paediatric ADHD, not about this enzyme pathway.
assessment.limitations: Boys only; no enzyme activity, flux, cysteine, stress-reactivity, or treatment endpoint.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Cysteine release is not a recovery measurement
scientific_findings.finding_summary: The pathway releases cysteine. Later glutathione synthesis can use that cysteine, but the assessed enzyme evidence does not measure recovery capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: An indirect biological bridge to recovery is not a recovery outcome and is not a treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Cysteine produced by cystathionine cleavage can supply later glutathione synthesis, but the assessed evidence does not measure recovery capacity.

content:
## BRS2-2-5 - Transsulfuration Pathway (Converting Homocysteine and Serine into Cysteine) ## 1. Mission & Overview ### Mission Divert homocysteine toward cysteine so methylation demand is balanced against sulfur amino-acid and redox needs. **Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Dominant Vitamin B6 supplies an essential enzyme cofactor. Comparative intervention dominance and benefit from additional intake are not established; moderate restriction altered cystathionine handling without lowering total pathway flux. [[7]](#pm-ref-7)
- Pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP; active vitamin B6 cofactor) - Vitamin B6
- Homocysteine - Serine - Cystathionine
- Combined folate/choline donor availability - Methionine-cycle sulfur supply #### Individual KC inputs - Methionine
### Overview Cystathionine beta-synthase joins homocysteine and serine to form cystathionine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) Cystathionine gamma-lyase then cleaves cystathionine and releases cysteine. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) Both enzymes require pyridoxal 5′-phosphate, the active cofactor made from vitamin B6. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) This irreversible branch disposes of homocysteine and produces cysteine. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) Studies of the purified enzymes establish these reactions and the cofactor requirement. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) - **Benefits:** Transsulfuration directs sulfur from homocysteine toward cysteine. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) Cells can later use that cysteine to make glutathione, which links this branch to antioxidant defence. - **Implementation Notes:** Vitamin B6 is the dietary source of pyridoxal 5′-phosphate. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) Homocysteine, serine, and cystathionine are substrates already in the pathway, not dietary targets. These enzyme studies do not show that eating more vitamin B6 speeds this conversion in people. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) - **Biological Relevance:** [Glutathione synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm6-glutathione-synthesis) is a later, separate use of the cysteine made here. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) ## 2. Primary Biological Effects ↑ cystathionine formation from homocysteine and serine
↑ cysteine release from cystathionine
↑ irreversible disposal of homocysteine through this branch ## 3. Intervention Levers
No preparation, supplement, fasting, or circadian practice assessed here has been shown to change this homocysteine-to-cysteine conversion.
No sleep, activity, or stress-recovery practice assessed here has been shown to change this homocysteine-to-cysteine conversion.
## 4. Mechanistic Basis ### Summary Homocysteine can leave the methyl cycle when it is joined to serine and the product is cleaved to cysteine. Those two enzyme steps set the chemistry of this conversion. They do not, by themselves, show how a change in vitamin B6 intake changes the rate in people.
#### (Homocysteine and serine become cystathionine) Cystathionine beta-synthase condenses L-homocysteine and L-serine to L-cystathionine. The reaction requires pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP), the active cofactor form of vitamin B6 [Belew et al. (2009) [[1]](#pm-ref-1); Meier et al. (2001) [[2]](#pm-ref-2)]. Both amino acids are substrates. Homocysteine is the sulfur amino acid coming from the methionine cycle. Serine is the cosubstrate that CBS condenses with it. #### (Cystathionine cleavage releases cysteine) Cystathionine gamma-lyase (CGL; also called CSE) is PLP-dependent and cleaves L-cystathionine in the step that produces cysteine [Zhu et al. (2008) [[3]](#pm-ref-3); Steegborn et al. (1999) [[4]](#pm-ref-4)]. Recombinant enzyme work shows strong gamma-lyase activity toward L-cystathionine and only marginal activity toward L-cysteine [[4]](#pm-ref-4). Cysteine is the product. It is not a substrate of this conversion. #### (Vitamin B6 supplies the cofactor) Food vitamin B6 is recycled to PLP by pyridoxal kinase, pyridoxine 5'-phosphate oxidase, and phosphatases [di Salvo et al. (2012) [[5]](#pm-ref-5)]. That salvage route explains why vitamin B6 matters to both enzymes. It does not measure how fast CBS or cystathionine gamma-lyase runs, and it does not show that a larger vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation. #### (Boundaries of the mechanism) This conversion is the irreversible route from homocysteine and serine, through cystathionine, to cysteine. Remethylation of homocysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM1-PM1 — Folate/B12-Dependent Homocysteine Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) and [BRS2-FM1-PM2 — Betaine/BHMT Remethylation](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation). SAMe formation and whole-cycle throughput belong to [BRS2-FM1-PM3 — SAMe Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm3-same-synthesis) and [BRS2-FM1-PM4 — Methionine Cycle Flux](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm4-methionine-cycle-flux). Glutathione synthesis from cysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM2-PM6 — Glutathione Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm6-glutathione-synthesis). Later antioxidant use of glutathione belongs with [BRS3 — Inflammation & Oxidative Stress](/docs/biological-targets/inflammation-oxidative-stress). #### (Integration within BRS2) Within [BRS2(FM2) — Transsulfuration & Redox Coupling](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-transsulfuration-redox-coupling), this conversion releases the cysteine that glutathione synthesis can use. Homocysteine that is not remethylated is the sulfur substrate of the first step. The split between remethylation and this branch is not measured on this page.
### 4.1 Scientific Findings #### Summary Purified and recombinant human enzyme studies establish the two transsulfuration reaction boundaries and their PLP dependence: CBS forms cystathionine, and CGL uses it to release cysteine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) [[3]](#pm-ref-3) The findings converge on biochemical pathway identity, including cysteine’s position as a product of the second step. They do not measure whole-body dietary responsiveness or glutathione synthesis, so neither increased flux from extra vitamin B6 nor downstream benefit is established by these assays. Human tracer evidence adds a physiological boundary: moderate vitamin B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling without significantly changing total transsulfuration. [[7]](#pm-ref-7) ## 5. BRS Pathways and Connections ### 5.1 BRS Pathways [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) ↓ [BRS2-FM2-PM6 — Glutathione Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm6-glutathione-synthesis) ### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships - None listed ### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships - [BRS2-FM2-PM6 — Glutathione Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm6-glutathione-synthesis) — Cysteine released when cystathionine is cleaved is the sulfur amino acid consumed when glutathione is assembled. Assembly of glutathione, and the redox reactions that spend it, sit outside this conversion. ## 7. Phenome Connections These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

Each Phenome relationship has two independent ratings. They are not combined or averaged.

Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength

How direct and important is this biological mechanism expected to be to the Phenome within the BRAIN model?

Evidence Confidence

How strongly does the adjudicated evidence support this particular biology → Phenome relationship?

Stress Reactivity — modulates Open Page → →
- **Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength:** Low–Medium - **Evidence Confidence:** Low–Medium - **Rationale:** Homocysteine can be joined to serine and then cleaved to cysteine, but that chemistry is not evidence of a stress-reactivity effect. A study of boys with ADHD found higher serum homocysteine and lower vitamin B12. It did not measure these enzymes, cysteine production, or stress outcomes, and it is not a treatment result Lukovac et al. (2024) [[6]](#pm-ref-6). **Supporting evidence**
Recovery Capacity — indirect Open Page → →
- **Biology → Phenome Relationship Strength:** Low - **Evidence Confidence:** Low - **Rationale:** Cysteine released by cystathionine cleavage can be used later for glutathione synthesis, which is a separate mechanism. The enzyme studies do not measure recovery capacity, and they do not show that changing this conversion treats recovery Zhu et al. (2008) [[3]](#pm-ref-3); Steegborn et al. (1999) [[4]](#pm-ref-4). **Supporting evidence**
## 8. References - [1] [Belew et al. (2009) — Human CBS kinetics with serine and homocysteine](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#belew_cbs_kinetics_2009) - [2] [Meier et al. (2001) — Human CBS structure and PLP dependence](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#meier_cbs_structure_2001) - [3] [Zhu et al. (2008) — Human CGL kinetics and PLP cofactor](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#zhu_cgl_kinetics_2008) - [4] [Steegborn et al. (1999) — Human CGL cleavage of cystathionine](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#steegborn_cgl_kinetics_1999) - [5] [di Salvo et al. (2012) — Vitamin B6 salvage to pyridoxal phosphate](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#disalvo_plp_availability_2012) - [6] [Lukovac et al. (2024) — Homocysteine biomarkers in paediatric ADHD](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#lukovac_serum_2024) - [7] [Lamers et al. (2011) — Moderate vitamin B6 restriction and transsulfuration kinetics](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#lamers_vitamin_b6_methionine_cycle_2011) - [8] [McCorvie et al. (2014) — SAM Activation of Human CBS](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#mccorvie_cbs_sam_activation_2014) - [9] [Liu et al. (2012) — Combined Donor Deprivation and Hepatic CBS Capacity](/docs/papers/BRAIN-Diet-References#liu_betaine_folate_2012)

title: Glutathione Synthesis
mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.
rationale: GCL/GSS substrate roles are supported in existing assessments. Sulphur-AA deprivation, combined NAC/glycine exposure and adequate-methionine cysteine null are distinct. Free cysteine versus cystine composition, glutamate/glutamine hydrolysis and ordinary-food substrate coverage remain unresolved; no fabricated food equivalence.

data.title: Glutathione Synthesis
data.mission: Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism.
data.summary: Cells assemble glutathione, the main intracellular thiol, in two ATP-dependent steps. Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine, then glutathione synthetase adds glycine. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis in healthy young men. Combined precursor supplements raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. These tracer studies measured synthesis in blood cells, not in the brain.
key_constraints: BRS2(KC2) - Methionine–Cysteine Sulfur Amino Acid Pool

pm_kc_relationships.dietary_input_note: Pool/constraint dependency, not another dietary constituent. Dietary supply decisions belong to its separately admitted PM input atoms.
pm_kc_relationships.pm_biological_role: Removing methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis, and removing cysteine alone did not when methionine stayed adequate. That is the sulfur-amino-acid provision relationship already recorded for cysteine and methionine.
pm_kc_relationships.evidence_limitation: Lyons used a 10-day amino-acid formula that removed both methionine and cysteine in healthy young men, and whole-blood glutathione concentration was maintained. Courtney-Martin kept methionine adequate and found that removing cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men. Neither study identifies a bottleneck beyond those provision relationships. This is not neuronal synthesis, ordinary mixed-diet advice, or a benefit from increasing an adequate intake.

presentation_review.rationale: Sulfur-amino-acid provision sustaining glutathione synthesis is cysteine as the direct assembly substrate and methionine as its precursor. A resource-dependency label and a KC2 origin tag do not create a further biological job. Lyons supplies the combined-depletion bound and Courtney-Martin the adequate-methionine bound. No additional competition, allocation, or other bottleneck was measured.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains glutathione synthesis capacity.
established_links: Glutamate-cysteine ligase uses cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine (PM6-F1).
A diet containing neither methionine nor cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione fractional and absolute synthesis in healthy young men, while glycine intake was not reduced (PM6-F2).
With methionine held at an adequate intake, cysteine intakes from zero upward did not change erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in young men (PM6-F2).
inferred_links: Ordinary mixed diets are commonly short of this pool.
The same synthesis-rate change occurs in neurons or in clinical populations.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: KC2 applicability stays established because these sulfur-amino-acid studies bear on glutathione synthesis. The public disclosure is consolidated as a duplicate of PM6-DIT-1 and PM6-DIT-9. Lyons is combined depletion. Courtney-Martin is the adequate-methionine boundary. Neither study measures a competition, allocation, or other bottleneck beyond that provision.

data.dose_sensitivity: Cysteine, glutamate and glycine are assembly substrates. Combined precursor supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults only; that is not general dietary advice. Selenium and riboflavin are not synthesis requirements.

phenome_relationships.rationale: Glutathione assembly supplies a thiol used in cellular redox buffering, which is relevant to recovery only as downstream biology. The human synthesis measurements are erythrocyte kinetics after combined precursor supplementation in older adults, not a recovery-outcome trial {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011}}. A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis while concentration was maintained {{cite:lyons_glutathione_2000}}. Higher homocysteine in boys with ADHD does not measure glutathione synthesis or recovery {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

The same thiol pool is a plausible contributor to stress buffering, but no assessed study tested a stress-resilience outcome {{cite:sekhar_glutathione_2011,lyons_glutathione_2000}}. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience {{cite:lukovac_serum_2024}}.

data.scientific_findings_intro: Human tracer studies show context-dependent substrate responsiveness. Removing methionine and cysteine together reduced whole-blood glutathione synthesis, whereas removing cysteine with methionine kept adequate did not reduce erythrocyte synthesis in young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) In older adults with lower baseline synthesis, combined N-acetylcysteine and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These contrasts support provision under defined conditions, not universal dietary cysteine limitation; blood-cell measurements do not establish neuronal synthesis or clinical benefit.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Two ATP-dependent enzymes assemble glutathione
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Glutamate-cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine using ATP. Glutathione synthetase then adds glycine, again using ATP, and binds magnesium. Selenium-dependent peroxidase activity and riboflavin-derived FAD in glutathione reductase are not part of these assembly reactions.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Glutamate, cysteine, glycine and ATP are the assembly substrates. Magnesium participates in the second enzyme. ATP and magnesium are intracellular biochemical requirements, not dietary levers. Selenium and riboflavin support later use and recycling of glutathione.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Glutathione synthesis requires ATP-dependent formation of γ-glutamylcysteine from glutamate and cysteine, followed by ATP-dependent addition of glycine, and does not use selenium or riboflavin as synthesis substrates.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Reviewed catalytic annotation of purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase records ATP-dependent ligation of L-glutamate and L-cysteine as the first step. Human glutathione synthetase structural work records ATP-dependent addition of glycine and one bound magnesium ion per subunit as the second step. Together they define the assembly boundary. Human glutathione peroxidase uses an active-site selenocysteine to reduce peroxides with glutathione already formed, and glutathione reductase binds FAD while reducing glutathione disulfide. Those enzymes consume or restore glutathione; they do not assemble it.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: The enzyme evidence is purified protein and structure, not intact human flux. A lower cysteine Km on the first enzyme does not prove that ordinary diets are cysteine-limited. Magnesium binding does not show that magnesium intake changes synthesis. The dietary review that groups selenium and riboflavin with glutathione support does not move those cofactors into the assembly reactions.

evidence_considered.label: Misra and Griffith (1998)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Purified human glutamate-cysteine ligase catalyses ATP-dependent ligation of L-glutamate and L-cysteine, the first step of glutathione biosynthesis.

assessment.study: Expression and purification of human gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase, with catalytic constants recorded in the reviewed human GCLC entry that cites this paper.
assessment.population: Purified human enzyme; no human participants.
assessment.result: The reaction consumes L-glutamate, L-cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine, ADP and phosphate. The cited annotation reports Km values of 0.1 mM for L-cysteine, 1.8 mM for L-glutamate and 0.4 mM for ATP.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Purified-enzyme Km values only; no human synthesis-rate effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human-enzyme evidence for the first ATP-dependent assembly step and its amino-acid and ATP substrates.
assessment.limitations: In-vitro constants do not establish in-vivo limitation, dietary responsiveness, tissue differences or clinical effects.

evidence_considered.label: Polekhina et al. (1999)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Human glutathione synthetase produces glutathione from γ-glutamylcysteine and glycine in an ATP-dependent reaction and binds one magnesium ion per subunit.

assessment.study: Crystal structure of human glutathione synthetase at 2.10 Å in complex with ADP and glutathione, with catalytic and cofactor annotation.
assessment.population: Crystallised human glutathione synthetase; no human participants.
assessment.result: The structure and catalytic annotation place glycine and ATP in the second assembly step and record one Mg2+ ion bound per subunit.
assessment.effect_magnitude: 2.10 Å structure; no physiological effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct structural evidence for the second ATP-dependent step and its magnesium ion.
assessment.limitations: A product-bound structure establishes catalytic participants, not dietary dose response or in-vivo flux.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Minich et al. (2019)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Reviews dietary nutrients discussed for glutathione support, including sulfur amino acids, selenium and riboflavin.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: It is a narrative review and does not itself measure the ligase reactions, ATP use, or separation of assembly from peroxidase and reductase cofactors.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Mullenbach et al. (1987)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Shows that human glutathione peroxidase encodes an active-site selenocysteine, so selenium belongs to peroxide removal that uses glutathione.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Peroxidase activity consumes glutathione. It is not a substrate or cofactor of either assembly enzyme.

connected_supportive_evidence.label: Karplus and Schulz (1989)
connected_supportive_evidence.why_relevant: Glutathione reductase structures show bound FAD, the riboflavin-derived cofactor, at the enzyme that reduces glutathione disulfide.
connected_supportive_evidence.why_excluded: Disulfide reduction is recycling of glutathione already made. FAD is not a substrate of glutamate-cysteine ligase or glutathione synthetase.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Blood-cell synthesis responds only under defined substrate conditions
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Removing both methionine and cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young men. Combined cysteine-precursor and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. A methionine-adequate diet without cysteine did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Substrate supply can change blood-cell synthesis in these specific conditions. That does not mean every ordinary diet is cysteine-limited, and the older-adult result is a supplemental precursor plus glycine, not a food prescription.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Human blood-cell glutathione synthesis can slow when dietary methionine and cysteine are both removed and can rise in older adults after combined cysteine and glycine precursor supplementation, whereas a methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not limit erythrocyte synthesis in young men.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Three human tracer studies set the ceiling. In seven healthy young men, a 10-day amino-acid diet with methionine and cysteine removed lowered whole-blood fractional synthesis from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day and lowered absolute synthesis by about 23%, while concentration stayed near 1.2 mM and glycine intake was not reduced. In eight older adults compared with eight younger adults, erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and concentration were lower, and two weeks of cysteine plus glycine precursor supplementation raised fractional synthesis by 78.8% and absolute synthesis by 230.9%. The cysteine source in that protocol is N-acetylcysteine, given with glycine. In four young men, cysteine intakes from zero to 40 mg/kg/day did not change erythrocyte synthesis when methionine was held at 14 mg/kg/day. Synthesis is therefore substrate-responsive under defined restrictions, not universally limited by dietary cysteine.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

evidence_considered.label: Lyons et al. (2000)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: A sulfur-amino-acid-free amino-acid diet slowed whole-blood glutathione synthesis in healthy young men without lowering glutathione concentration.

assessment.study: Randomised crossover of two 10-day L-amino-acid diets, adequate versus methionine and cysteine both set to zero, with a primed intravenous L-[1-13C]cysteine infusion on day 10.
assessment.population: Seven healthy men, age 24 ± 6 years.
assessment.result: Fractional synthesis fell from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day (P < 0.01). Absolute synthesis fell from 747 ± 216 to 578.6 ± 135 µmol/L/day (P < 0.05), about 23%. Whole-blood glutathione stayed about 1.2 mM (1,142 ± 243 versus 1,216 ± 162 µM). Glycine in the formula rose from 39.6 to 75.1 mg/kg/day so nitrogen stayed constant; glutamic acid was unchanged.
assessment.effect_magnitude: About a 23% lower absolute synthesis rate after 10 days without methionine and cysteine; concentration unchanged.
assessment.evidence_summary: Direct human evidence that removing the shared sulfur-amino-acid supply slows whole-blood glutathione synthesis.
assessment.limitations: Experimental formula, young men, short duration, whole blood rather than brain, and no clinical outcome. Glycine was increased, so the slowdown is not a glycine deficit.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Older adults had lower erythrocyte glutathione synthesis than younger adults, and two weeks of cysteine plus glycine precursor supplementation restored synthesis and concentration.

assessment.study: Stable-isotope erythrocyte glutathione kinetics before and after precursor supplementation. Cysteine was supplied as N-acetylcysteine together with glycine.
assessment.population: Eight older adults restudied after supplementation, compared with eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Before supplementation, older adults had lower erythrocyte glycine, cysteine, glutathione concentration, fractional synthesis (45.80 ± 5.69 versus 83.14 ± 6.43 %/day) and absolute synthesis (0.55 ± 0.12 versus 1.73 ± 0.16 mmol/L red cells per day). After two weeks, glutathione concentration was 94.6% higher, fractional synthesis 78.8% higher and absolute synthesis 230.9% higher, and plasma oxidative-stress markers were lower.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Combined precursor supplementation in older adults: fractional synthesis +78.8% and absolute synthesis +230.9% from the deficient baseline.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human evidence that combined supplemental cysteine precursor and glycine can raise erythrocyte glutathione synthesis when it is low in older adults.
assessment.limitations: Small older-adult sample, erythrocyte pool, combined supplements, not ordinary food, not neuronal synthesis, and not an ADHD or recovery trial.

evidence_considered.label: Courtney-Martin et al. (2008)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis did not change across cysteine intakes, including zero, when methionine intake was adequate.

assessment.study: Five graded cysteine intakes (0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 mg/kg/day) in random order with methionine fixed at 14 mg/kg/day and protein at 1 g/kg/day. Erythrocyte glutathione synthesis was measured after two days at each intake.
assessment.population: Four healthy young adult men.
assessment.result: Fractional and absolute erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and glutathione concentration did not change as cysteine intake increased. Urinary sulfate excretion rose with cysteine intake (r = 0.92).
assessment.effect_magnitude: No change in erythrocyte glutathione synthesis across the cysteine range tested.
assessment.evidence_summary: Human evidence that dietary cysteine is not independently limiting for erythrocyte glutathione synthesis when methionine intake meets the protein requirement.
assessment.limitations: Preliminary sample of four men, two-day adaptation, erythrocyte endpoint, and no neuronal or clinical outcome.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is also used in PM6-F3 and PM6-F4 for the phenome boundary, and in PM6-IC1 for the measurement boundary. Those uses are not independent replications of the synthesis-rate result.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Blood-cell glutathione kinetics are not neuronal synthesis or clinical outcome
scientific_findings.finding_statement: Erythrocyte and whole-blood glutathione synthesis rates and concentrations do not measure neuronal glutathione synthesis, do not establish that every person is substrate-limited, and are not ADHD, recovery or stress-resilience outcomes.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The human tracer studies measure incorporation of labelled cysteine or glycine into glutathione in whole blood or red cells. In the sulfur-amino-acid-free diet, synthesis slowed while concentration was maintained, so concentration is not a substitute for synthesis rate. None of the studies sampled brain glutathione synthesis or tested a recovery, stress or ADHD outcome. A paediatric ADHD study that found higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 did not measure glutathione.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This constraint limits interpretation. It does not prove that neuronal synthesis is unrelated to substrate supply, and it does not reclassify the blood-cell synthesis results themselves.

evidence_considered.label: Lyons et al. (2000)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Whole-blood synthesis rate changed while glutathione concentration did not, and the measurement was not a brain or clinical endpoint.

assessment.study: Sulfur-amino-acid-free versus adequate amino-acid diets with whole-blood glutathione kinetics.
assessment.population: Seven healthy young men.
assessment.result: Synthesis slowed and concentration was maintained. No neuronal or symptom endpoint was measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Concentration unchanged despite about a 23% lower absolute synthesis rate.
assessment.evidence_summary: Shows that blood glutathione concentration and blood synthesis rate are different measurements.
assessment.limitations: Does not describe neuronal glutathione.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Erythrocyte synthesis and oxidative-stress markers changed in older adults; the study did not measure brain synthesis or an ADHD outcome.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers before and after precursor supplementation.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Erythrocyte synthesis and concentration rose in the older group after supplementation. No ADHD, recovery or stress-resilience outcome was tested.
assessment.effect_magnitude: Erythrocyte fractional synthesis +78.8% in the supplemented older group.
assessment.evidence_summary: The supported endpoint is older-adult erythrocyte synthesis, not a universal or clinical claim.
assessment.limitations: Blood-cell kinetics in a small older-adult sample.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Boys with ADHD had higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12 than controls; glutathione was not measured.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarkers and behavioural scores in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years, 67 with ADHD and 66 controls.
assessment.result: Homocysteine was higher and vitamin B12 lower in the ADHD group. Glutathione synthesis was not an endpoint.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No glutathione concentration or synthesis rate was reported.
assessment.evidence_summary: An ADHD biomarker association that does not measure this synthesis reaction.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional, boys only, no glutathione assay, and no dietary intervention.

evidence_dependency: Lyons et al. (2000) and Sekhar et al. (2011) are primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2. PM6-IC1 uses them only to bound what those measurements can mean.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Recovery-capacity benefit is not established
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Glutathione assembly is biologically relevant to redox buffering, but the assessed studies do not show that changing synthesis improves Recovery Capacity.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Older-adult erythrocyte synthesis and a paediatric homocysteine difference must not be read as recovery treatment evidence.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Recovery Capacity as a functional or clinical outcome.
scientific_findings.synthesis: The older-adult trial changed erythrocyte glutathione synthesis and plasma oxidative-stress markers after combined precursor supplementation. It did not measure recovery capacity. The paediatric ADHD study measured homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis and not recovery. The relationship remains a mechanistic possibility with a direct-evidence gap.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: This is a gap in the assessed evidence, not proof that no relationship exists. Oxidative-stress markers are not a recovery phenome.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Precursor supplementation raised erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in older adults and lowered oxidative-stress markers, without a recovery outcome.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Synthesis and glutathione concentration rose in the older group. Recovery capacity was not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No recovery-outcome effect size exists in the study.
assessment.evidence_summary: Supports a synthesis change, not a recovery-capacity benefit.
assessment.limitations: Wrong endpoint for this phenome relationship.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: ADHD was associated with higher homocysteine and lower vitamin B12, not with a glutathione or recovery measurement.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarker comparison in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years.
assessment.result: Homocysteine and vitamin B12 differed by ADHD status. Glutathione and recovery were not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No glutathione or recovery effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Does not test this phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional biomarker study in boys.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2. Its use here is only to show that the trial did not measure Recovery Capacity.

scientific_findings.finding_label: Stress-resilience benefit is not established
scientific_findings.finding_summary: Substrate-responsive glutathione synthesis is relevant to redox buffering, but none of the assessed studies tested Stress Resilience.
scientific_findings.finding_interpretation: Do not convert blood-cell synthesis changes or an ADHD homocysteine difference into a stress-resilience treatment claim.
scientific_findings.finding_statement: The assessed human evidence does not demonstrate that glutathione synthesis capacity changes Stress Resilience.
scientific_findings.synthesis: Sulfur-amino-acid removal and older-adult precursor supplementation changed blood-cell glutathione synthesis. Neither study measured stress resilience. The paediatric ADHD biomarker study did not measure glutathione or stress resilience. The phenome link stays mechanistic and untested.
scientific_findings.synthesis_limitations: Absence of a direct test is not evidence against a biological contribution. It does block treatment and dietary-advice claims.

evidence_considered.label: Sekhar et al. (2011)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: Older-adult erythrocyte glutathione synthesis rose after precursor supplementation, with no stress-resilience endpoint.

assessment.study: Erythrocyte glutathione kinetics and plasma oxidative-stress markers.
assessment.population: Eight older adults and eight younger adults.
assessment.result: Erythrocyte synthesis changed. Stress resilience was not measured.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No stress-resilience effect size.
assessment.evidence_summary: Synthesis evidence without a stress-resilience outcome.
assessment.limitations: Endpoint mismatch for this phenome.

evidence_considered.label: Lukovac et al. (2024)
evidence_considered.directional_finding: The ADHD cohort difference was in homocysteine and vitamin B12, not glutathione synthesis or stress resilience.

assessment.study: Cross-sectional serum biomarkers in boys with and without ADHD.
assessment.population: 133 boys aged 6.5–12.5 years.
assessment.result: Homocysteine and vitamin B12 differed. Stress resilience and glutathione were not endpoints.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No stress-resilience or glutathione effect.
assessment.evidence_summary: Does not test the phenome relationship.
assessment.limitations: Cross-sectional paediatric biomarker study.

evidence_dependency: Sekhar et al. (2011) is primary synthesis evidence in PM6-F2 and is reused here only for the missing stress-resilience endpoint. Lukovac et al. (2024) is also primary evidence in PM6-F3 and PM6-IC1.

decision.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains glutathione synthesis capacity.
established_links: Glutamate-cysteine ligase uses cysteine and ATP to form γ-glutamylcysteine (PM6-F1).
A diet containing neither methionine nor cysteine slowed whole-blood glutathione fractional and absolute synthesis in healthy young men, while glycine intake was not reduced (PM6-F2).
With methionine held at an adequate intake, cysteine intakes from zero upward did not change erythrocyte glutathione synthesis in young men (PM6-F2).
inferred_links: Ordinary mixed diets are commonly short of this pool.
The same synthesis-rate change occurs in neurons or in clinical populations.
decision.rationale: KC2 applicability stays established because these sulfur-amino-acid studies bear on glutathione synthesis. The public disclosure is consolidated as a duplicate of PM6-DIT-1 and PM6-DIT-9. Lyons is combined depletion. Courtney-Martin is the adequate-methionine boundary. Neither study measures a competition, allocation, or other bottleneck beyond that provision.

kc_adjudication_history.rationale: Metadata migration only: preserve the established governs/constrained-by interpretation as a typed Conditional constraint for FM summary derivation. No stronger scientific admission.

content:
## BRS2-2-6 - Glutathione Synthesis (Assembling glutathione from glutamate, cysteine and glycine) ## 1. Mission & Overview + Dietary Levers ### Mission Build glutathione from sulfur amino acids so cellular antioxidant defence stays connected to one-carbon metabolism. **Intervention Dominance:** Diet-Dominant
- Cysteine - Methionine - Glutamate - Glycine - N-acetylcysteine
- ATP - Magnesium ions (Mg²⁺)
No mapping established.
### Overview Cells assemble glutathione, the main intracellular thiol, in two ATP-dependent steps. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins glutamate and cysteine, then glutathione synthetase adds glycine. [[1]](#pm-ref-1) [[2]](#pm-ref-2) A sulfur-amino-acid-free diet slowed whole-blood synthesis in healthy young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) Combined precursor supplements raised erythrocyte synthesis in older adults. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These tracer studies measured synthesis in blood cells, not in the brain. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) - **Benefits:** Cells draw on this thiol to limit oxidative stress. In older adults, higher blood-cell synthesis after precursor supplements came with lower plasma oxidative-stress markers. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) That thiol is how sulfur amino acids from one-carbon metabolism stay connected to cellular antioxidant defence. - **Implementation Notes:** Cysteine, methionine, glutamate, glycine, and N-acetylcysteine are the provision routes. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[4]](#pm-ref-4) A methionine-adequate cysteine-free diet did not lower erythrocyte synthesis in young men, so these results do not set a routine dose. [[5]](#pm-ref-5) - **Biological Relevance:** Clearing peroxides and recycling oxidised glutathione are separate from this assembly. [[8]](#pm-ref-8) [[9]](#pm-ref-9) ## 2. Primary Biological Effects ↑ glutathione formation from glutamate, cysteine and glycine
↑ γ-glutamylcysteine as the intermediate of the first step
→ later peroxide removal and glutathione recycling remain outside this reaction ## 3. Intervention Levers
No preparation method, supplement schedule, or fasting pattern has been shown to change these two assembly reactions.
No sleep, activity, or stress-recovery behaviour has been shown to change these assembly reactions. Cells make the ATP the enzymes use, but that has not been tied to a lifestyle lever for glutathione synthesis.
## 4. Mechanistic Basis ### Summary Glutathione formation is the point at which glutamate, cysteine and glycine become the cell's main low-molecular-weight thiol. The defining events are the two ATP-dependent assembly steps. Making the cysteine, and later using or recycling the glutathione, are separate processes.
#### (Two ATP-dependent assembly steps) Glutathione (GSH; γ-glutamylcysteinylglycine) is built in two steps that each use ATP (the cell's energy-carrying molecule). Glutamate–cysteine ligase joins the side-chain carboxyl of glutamate to cysteine, forming γ-glutamylcysteine (a two-amino-acid intermediate) [[1]](#pm-ref-1). Glutathione synthetase then adds glycine, and the human enzyme binds one magnesium ion per subunit [[2]](#pm-ref-2). The reviewed constants for the purified first enzyme give cysteine a lower Km (0.1 mM) than glutamate (1.8 mM) [[1]](#pm-ref-1). That biochemical preference is not the same thing as a universal dietary cysteine shortage. #### (When human blood-cell synthesis changes) In seven healthy young men, removing methionine and cysteine from an otherwise adequate amino-acid formula for 10 days lowered whole-blood fractional synthesis from 0.65 ± 0.13 to 0.49 ± 0.13 per day and lowered absolute synthesis by about 23%, while glutathione concentration stayed near 1.2 mM. Glycine in that formula was increased, not reduced [[3]](#pm-ref-3). In older adults, erythrocyte synthesis was lower than in younger adults and rose after two weeks of a cysteine precursor, supplied as N-acetylcysteine, together with glycine [[4]](#pm-ref-4). When methionine was held at 14 mg/kg/day, cysteine intakes from zero to 40 mg/kg/day did not change erythrocyte synthesis in four young men [[5]](#pm-ref-5). #### (What is outside the assembly reactions) Selenium is part of glutathione peroxidase: human glutathione peroxidase uses an active-site selenocysteine and glutathione to reduce peroxides [[8]](#pm-ref-8). Riboflavin is relevant because glutathione reductase binds FAD, a riboflavin-derived cofactor, while it reduces oxidised glutathione back to the reduced form [[9]](#pm-ref-9). A dietary review groups these nutrients with glutathione support [[6]](#pm-ref-6). They act after glutathione has been made. #### (Boundaries of the mechanism) This reaction is glutathione assembly from glutamate, cysteine and glycine. Conversion of homocysteine to cysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway). Remethylation of homocysteine belongs to [BRS2-FM1-PM1](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm1-folate-b12-dependent-homocysteine-remethylation) and [BRS2-FM1-PM2](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm1/brs2-fm1-pm2-betaine-bhmt-remethylation). Using glutathione to limit lipid peroxidation belongs to [BRS3-FM2-PM5 — Lipid Peroxidation Control](/docs/biological-targets/brs3/fm2/brs3-fm2-pm5-lipid-peroxidation-control). #### (Integration within BRS2) Within [BRS2(FM2) — Transsulfuration & Redox Coupling](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-transsulfuration-redox-coupling), transsulfuration can supply cysteine and this reaction consumes it. Inadequacy of the shared methionine–cysteine pool can slow synthesis: whole-blood synthesis fell when both amino acids were removed [[3]](#pm-ref-3). That does not make selenium, riboflavin, or a clinical treatment part of the assembly step.
### 4.1 Scientific Findings #### Summary Human tracer studies show context-dependent substrate responsiveness. Removing methionine and cysteine together reduced whole-blood glutathione synthesis, whereas removing cysteine with methionine kept adequate did not reduce erythrocyte synthesis in young men. [[3]](#pm-ref-3) [[5]](#pm-ref-5) In older adults with lower baseline synthesis, combined N-acetylcysteine and glycine supplementation raised erythrocyte synthesis. [[4]](#pm-ref-4) These contrasts support provision under defined conditions, not universal dietary cysteine limitation; blood-cell measurements do not establish neuronal synthesis or clinical benefit. ## 5. BRS Pathways and Connections ### 5.1 BRS Pathways [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) ↓ [BRS2-FM2-PM6 — Glutathione Synthesis](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm6-glutathione-synthesis) ### 5.2 Cross-BRS Mechanism Relationships Primary Mechanisms in other Biological Regulatory Systems that directly interact with, constrain or support this mechanism. - [BRS3-FM2-PM5 — Lipid Peroxidation Control](/docs/biological-targets/brs3/fm2/brs3-fm2-pm5-lipid-peroxidation-control) — Glutathione made by these assembly steps can later be consumed when peroxides are reduced. That peroxide removal, glutathione recycling, and selenium-dependent peroxidase activity are downstream of assembly. ### 5.3 Local BRS Mechanism Relationships Related Primary Mechanisms within the same Biological Regulatory System that collectively support the integrated biological function. - [BRS2-FM2-PM5 — Transsulfuration Pathway](/docs/biological-targets/brs2/fm2/brs2-fm2-pm5-transsulfuration-pathway) — Converts homocysteine into cysteine that the first assembly step can use. This is upstream sulfur-amino-acid supply, not the ATP-dependent reactions that form glutathione. ## 7. Phenome Connections These mappings are translational relationships, not single-mechanism outcome claims. Phenomes are emergent functional patterns supported by multiple interacting PMs across the BRAIN Framework.

title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
rationale: Kennedy and PEMT routes must remain separate; plasma PC/enrichment is not brain PC formation or total flux. Current route assessments preserved; additional form-specific dietary extraction deferred.

data.title: Phosphatidylcholine Formation
data.mission: Maintain phosphatidylcholine formation through PEMT methylation and the choline-based Kennedy pathway.
data.summary: Cells form phosphatidylcholine through distinct routes: hepatic PEMT methylates phosphatidylethanolamine using SAMe, while the Kennedy pathway combines choline-derived phosphocholine with CTP and then diacylglycerol. Uridine can contribute upstream to nucleotide supply. These routes support membrane phospholipid provision; precursor availability does not establish that extra intake increases human membrane synthesis or improves cognition.

evidence_qualification.label: Diet-Supported
evidence_qualification.rationale: The retained Diet-Supported qualification is supported by conditional PM-specific dietary influence; it does not establish comparative intervention dominance.
evidence_qualification.scope_note: Conditional animal evidence concerns folate restriction and methyl-derived PC enrichment; it does not establish absolute PEMT flux, benefit above adequacy or cognitive benefit.

routes.intervention_effect: Eight-week folate restriction with labelled choline maintained reduced hepatic d3-PC enrichment and the product/precursor enrichment ratio in female mice.
routes.context: Female wild-type and Mthfr-heterozygous mice; the hepatic response was not demonstrated in males.
routes.limitations: Enrichment is not absolute PEMT flux. The restriction experiment does not establish supplementation benefit above adequacy, a human intake target or cognitive benefit.

principal_route_selection.rationale: Dietary Requirements is the principal displayed route because the assessed folate-restriction intervention changed pathway-specific hepatic PC methyl enrichment, a mission-relevant endpoint. The measured conditional effect, rather than nutrient necessity or absence of competing levers, supports prominence. Precursor provision records explain the route but do not independently establish intervention responsiveness.
principal_route_selection.comparative_limitations: Dietary prominence is supported within the studied animal context; it is not a head-to-head ranking against lifestyle or optimisation, a human intake target, or evidence of benefit from extra intake.

assessments.relevance: PM7-F5 measures dietary methyl contribution to hepatic PC formation, directly relevant to the PEMT branch of this PM's mission.
assessments.directness: Chew 2011 experimentally restricted folate for eight weeks with choline maintained; female mice had reduced labelled PC enrichment and a lower product/precursor enrichment ratio. This is dietary manipulation, not an inference from nutrient presence.
assessments.extent: Hepatic d3-PC enrichment was 30% lower (P=0.017), with a lower d3-PC:d9-choline ratio (P=0.049). This supports substantial conditional dietary influence on the measured PEMT-related endpoint, not absolute flux or all PC synthesis. The hepatic response was not demonstrated in males, and no human or cognitive benefit is inferred.

data.dose_sensitivity: Dietary methyl-donor provision is supported; increasing intake is not established to increase absolute PEMT activity or improve cognition.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methyl-donor pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
established_links: KC1 defines folate, choline and betaine as a coherent remethylation donor pool; B12 remains an excluded cofactor.
Folate restriction with choline maintained reduced hepatic methyl-derived PC enrichment in female mice (PM7-F5).
Betaine restored reported PEMT-mediated production under ethanol-induced methylation imbalance (PM7-F5; abstract-level complementary evidence).
inferred_links: Absolute formation rate, universal donor limitation and human or cognitive benefit are not established.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Type D is met conditionally: named-donor restriction and complementary imbalance rescue connect this pool to pathway-specific formation. Enrichment is not absolute flux; a human or one end-to-end flux assay is not mandatory.

kc_applicability_adjudications.applicability_proposition: Inadequacy of the shared methionine and cysteine pool constrains hepatic PEMT-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation.
established_links: Dietary methionine supplies the upstream MAT/SAM route used by PEMT (PM7-F1/F6). This supported chain is not rejected for being upstream.
Shimada 2003 Table 4 separates methionine-associated phospholipid changes from cystine-associated growth rescue with choline held constant; PC:PE and SAM concentrations are not PEMT flux.

Asiriwardhana 2025 Figure 4C measures dietary methionine-dependent methyl incorporation into hepatic PC in neonatal piglets; cysteine was held constant. This closes the concentration-only endpoint gap.

Robinson 2016 primary abstract reports higher hepatic PC synthesis and lower creatine synthesis after donor removal with methionine restricted in both groups. Allocation is context-dependent, not uniform suppression.
Sugiyama 1995 primary abstract reports that eritadenine did not directly inhibit PEMT in the assay; the 1998 inhibitor comparison is not a selective PEMT blockade.
Cano 2011 indexed primary results and prior appraisal support altered PEMT activity after MAT1A deletion. Genetic SAM-production impairment is not dietary sulfur-pool inadequacy.
inferred_links: Whether methionine–cysteine pool availability creates a separately supported allocation, competition or other constraint on PEMT beyond the documented methionine-to-SAM provision job. Cysteine compensation and the relevant context remain unestablished for this proposition.
kc_applicability_adjudications.rationale: Retain the specified conditional-constraint proposition unresolved, while recognising supported upstream methionine provision and measured nutritional effects on methyl incorporation into PC. No human, universal deficiency or absolute-flux gate is imposed. Provision evidence does not by itself establish a distinct shared sulfur-pool bottleneck; donor restriction can redistribute synthesis rather than lower PC synthesis.
kc_applicability_adjudications.evidence_gap: Evidence linking the named methionine–cysteine pool, including cysteine compensation where relevant, to a constraint beyond methionine/SAM provision in a specified context. Sugiyama 1998 full methods and Cano 2011 full assay methods remain inaccessible in this pass; neither access gap is treated as proof of non-applicability.

phenome_relationships.rationale: SAMe-dependent phosphatidylcholine formation couples one-carbon methylation to membrane phospholipid chemistry — the methylation-dependent bridge between B-vitamin status and omega-3-enriched PC delivery toward the brain. VITACOG reanalysis, PEMT pathway biology, and phospholipid-bound DHA accretion evidence support cognitive-clarity framework translation. The findings support an association with cognitive outcomes, while the proposed causal role of methylation–membrane coupling remains unproven. Applicability to ADHD has not yet been established.

Diet and choline reviews discuss attention and neurodevelopment {{cite:millichap_diet_2012}} {{cite:derbyshire_role_2023}}. They do not measure PEMT activity. Piglet brain DHA accretion and human cerebrospinal-fluid DHA likewise do not record this methylation {{cite:liu_higher_2014}} {{cite:arellanes_brain_2020}}. Any attention relationship is a downstream inference.
